description: Phase routing for the main-leader -> bridge-window -> bridge-leader workflow. Phase legality is route-level; bridge/team/task lifecycle legality is owned by lifecycle_transition_table.json and workflow_runtime.py.

phases.name: leader_freeze
phases.description: Main-leader reads runtime truth, accepts new user input, and freezes execution-relevant semantics/scope.

phases.name: l2_advisory
phases.description: Optional advisory route for sharpening plan/semantics without downstream mutation.

phases.name: l3_bridge
phases.description: Main-leader may open exactly one bridge window per bridge invocation. Bridge-leader owns the team/task lifecycle inside that window.

phases.name: l4_implement
phases.description: Implementation-facing work requested through bridge windows.

phases.name: l4_execute
phases.description: Execution-facing work, validation, and postrun checks requested through bridge windows.

phases.name: l4_anomaly
phases.description: Recovery/anomaly route for failed, partial, blocked, or orphaned bridge windows.

global_rules.description: Main-leader must read runtime_snapshot before dispatching the next bridge invocation.
One bridge invocation window binds exactly one team and one task.
Main-leader does not directly create teams, tasks, or teammate messages.
Bridge-leader owns team_create, task_create, send_messages, task completion, and team_delete inside the bridge window.
Authoritative runtime mutation must pass through RuntimeEvent -> CheckResult -> UpdateResult -> NotifyResult.
Denied, failed, partial, timeout, and orphaned lifecycle facts must be persisted instead of erased.
If runtime diagnostics classify an open bridge window as a bridge orchestration hang, main-leader should stop ordinary waiting and diagnose through snapshot refs before retrying or rerouting.
